question.question: 뇌 신경이 서서히 망가지는 한 병입니다. 1817년 런던의 한 의사가 거리에서 본 환자를 포함해 여섯 사람의 사례를 모아 짧은 책을 냈습니다. 1877년 프랑스 신경학자 장마르탱 샤르코는 그 책이 붙인 병 이름이 모든 환자에게 맞지는 않는다며, 대신 그 의사의 이름으로 바꿔 불렀습니다. 이 병은?

facts.claim: 1817년 제임스 파킨슨 '떨림 마비에 관한 에세이' · 여섯 사례 · 셋은 런던 거리에서 · 1877년 샤르코가 떨림이 모두에게 있지 않아 개명
facts.note: In 1817, English physician James Parkinson published the first full medical description of the disease ... An Essay on the Shaking Palsy. He presented six clinical cases, including three he had observed on the streets near Hoxton Square in London. ... In 1877, Charcot renamed the disease after Parkinson, as the tremor suggested by "shaking palsy" is not present in all.

He is best known for his 1817 work An Essay on the Shaking Palsy, in which he was the first to describe "paralysis agitans", a condition that was later renamed Parkinson's disease by Jean-Martin Charcot.
Boxer Muhammad Ali showed signs of PD when he was 38 ... he has been called the "world's most famous Parkinson's patient".

facts.note: The patient's husband was the director of the boiler fabrication company Babcock and Wilcox ... The Renfrew company was a large user of industrial ultrasound that was used to check for crack and flaws in welds. Donald's purpose in making the visit to Renfrew on 21 July 1955 was to determine if the industrial detecting equipment could be used to differentiate types of tissue. facts.note: Scottish physician Ian Donald was one of the pioneers of medical use of ultrasound. His article "Investigation of Abdominal Masses by Pulsed Ultrasound" was published in The Lancet in 1958. Donald was Regius Professor of Midwifery at the University of Glasgow.

facts.note: In 1868, Adolf Kussmaul of Freiburg, Germany, performed an esophagoscopy on a sword-swallower using a rigid 47 cm (19 in) tube, mirrors, and a gasoline lamp. The apparatus, an early endoscope, allowed him to examine the esophagus and the fundus of the stomach.
Adolf Kussmaul was fascinated by sword swallowers who would insert a sword down their throat without gagging. This drew inspiration to insert a hollow tube for observation

The term endoscope was first used on February 7, 1855, by engineer-optician Charles Chevalier
